rewrites.headline: Westmark legislature passes Selby River water limits, 61-48
bullets: The bill caps agricultural water withdrawals from the Selby River basin during declared droughts.
Cities in the basin supported it; the state farm bureau opposed it.
The farm bureau estimates the cap could reduce irrigated acreage by about a fifth in drought years.
Governor Dana Ruiz has said she will sign the bill.
rewrites.whats_next: The farm bureau said it will challenge the law in court after it is signed.

rewrites.headline: Valdoria central bank holds benchmark rate at 4.25%
bullets: It is the third straight meeting with no change.
Inflation is 3.1%, above the bank's 2% target.
Two of seven board members voted for a cut, according to the bank's statement.
The bank said it expects inflation to ease toward its target next year.

rewrites.headline: Storm surge floods Port Avery; about 18,000 lose power
bullets: Seawater flooded the waterfront and downtown on Tuesday night.
No deaths were reported.
The mayor declared a local emergency.
The utility said some customers could be without power for two days.

rewrites.headline: Westmark ethics board reviews governor's use of state aircraft
bullets: The board confirmed a review of Governor Dana Ruiz's trips on state aircraft that included political events.
The review follows a complaint filed in October.
The governor's office said all trips were official business.

rewrites.headline: Westmark University regents delay vote on 9% tuition increase
bullets: Several hundred students rallied outside the regents' meeting against the proposal.
The increase would take effect next fall.
The regents moved the vote to December.

rewrites.headline: Brightline recalls about 42,000 e-bikes over battery overheating
bullets: The company received 31 reports of batteries overheating while charging, including four small fires.
Owners can get a free replacement battery.

rewrites.headline: Drought-tolerant wheat matches standard yields in three-year trial
bullets: The strain was developed at the Halvorsen Agricultural Institute.
Yields were similar to standard wheat over three years.
In the driest year, the new strain yielded 12% more.

rewrites.headline: Rural broadband grant recipients must report speeds and sign-ups
bullets: The Westmark Department of Commerce finalized the rule.
Recipients must report connection speeds and household sign-ups every six months.

rewrites.headline: Westmark Supreme Court rules mining company must fund old mine cleanup
bullets: The 5-2 ruling lets the state require Harlan Mining Co. to pay for cleaning up tailings ponds at mines closed before 1990.
A lower court will set the amount.

rewrites.headline: Westmark House passes rural hospital staffing bill, 70-39
bullets: The House passed H.B. 412, the Rural Hospital Staffing Act, by a recorded vote on November 3.

rewrites.headline: Westmark awards $48 million contract to repair 12 National Guard armories
bullets: The Department of Defense awarded the contract to Caldera Construction.
Work is expected to be completed in 2028.

rewrites.headline: Judge blocks Westmark voter ID rule until trial
bullets: District Judge Alma Reyes granted a preliminary injunction on Wednesday.
She found the challengers were likely to succeed on their claim that the rule was adopted without required public notice.
The rule will not apply in the March primary unless the ruling is overturned.
Voting rights groups brought the lawsuit. The secretary of state's office said it will appeal.

rewrites.headline: Westmark adds 14,200 jobs in October; unemployment holds at 4.1%
bullets: The figures come from the state Department of Labor's monthly report.
Manufacturing added 2,100 jobs.
Job growth slowed from 19,000 in September, according to the Metro Ledger.

rewrites.headline: Westmark will allow drone deliveries over neighborhoods
bullets: The state Department of Transportation finalized the rule.
Deliveries are allowed between 7 a.m. and 9 p.m., at least 200 feet up.

rewrites.headline: Valdoria and Ostria sign deal to phase out farm tariffs
bullets: The agreement removes tariffs on most agricultural goods over five years.
Both countries' parliaments must ratify it before it takes effect.

rewrites.headline: Kessland starts measles vaccinations after 120 cases
bullets: The health ministry is vaccinating children under 10.
Vaccines are offered free at schools, according to the Northside Tribune.

rewrites.headline: Northwind Health breach exposed records of 2.3 million patients
bullets: Names, birth dates and insurance numbers were accessed, the company said.
Northwind Health said no payment data was taken.
